Runners-up: (a) counting the 11 bolded definition entries as 11 coverage rows, when only 6 carry an availability verdict and 5 are quotas, hedges or pointers; (b) harvesting the 7 API bullets under 'General API support' as 7 supported apiOperation values, when the sentence only says they 'may have regional differences'; (c) reading the intro link as though this page enumerated GuardDuty's available Regions; (d) flattening 'AWS Dedicated Local Zones' and the 'aws' partition into the Region axis alongside ap-east-1/ap-east-2, mixing three different kinds of value; (e) losing the second dimension entirely - every statement here is per GuardDuty feature, protection plan or finding type, so an exclusion for RDS Protection says nothing about Malware Protection, and the shared DoH/DoT table applies to two finding types at once; (f) counting the 7 caveated finding types named across the page (CompromisedCredentials, BedrockLoggingDisabled, AnomalousModelInvocation, CostHarvesting, PromptInjection.Direct, UnusualDoHActivity, UnusualDoTActivity) as a findingType coverage catalogue - the page lists them as exceptions, not as a supported-finding-type list.
whatThePageStates: The page does NOT list the Regions where GuardDuty is available; it points to the Amazon Web Services General Reference for that list. Its only substance is one section, 'Region-specific feature availability', built as 11 bolded definition entries that each record an exception for one GuardDuty capability: a partition restriction on expanded filter fields, an API result-limit note, Malware Protection for EC2 in Dedicated Local Zones, two RDS Protection exclusions, three finding-type exclusion notes, an AI Protection dependency note, a list of 7 APIs that 'may have regional differences', and two pointer entries for GovCloud and China. Every coverage statement is an exception keyed to a named GuardDuty feature, protection plan or finding type, so the page is two-dimensional: Region (or partition) crossed with GuardDuty capability. Critically, the two entries that would carry the most values - the CompromisedCredentials exclusion list and the DoH/DoT exclusion table - are both replaced in this .md rendering by the placeholder link 'See the AWS documentation website for more details', so they enumerate zero Regions here. Nothing on the page states positive Region-by-Region support for GuardDuty as a whole.
